I'm 39, been farming our 6 mu in Quzhou for over twenty years. My husband works construction in Handan most of the year, so it's mainly me and my mother-in-law handling the fields day-to-day. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bags and I went to the county extension meeting last winter, but to be honest I trust what my own eyes see more than what some technician says in a classroom. I watch what my neighbors do — especially old Wang, whose family always gets good wheat — and I mostly stick with what worked before.

This year I'm keeping all 6 mu in wheat-maize double cropping. I thought about putting one mu into cotton because my cousin got a decent price last autumn, but cotton needs spraying every week in summer and my shoulders can't take that anymore. Wheat and maize are safer: the wheat gives us flour so we don't have to buy noodles, and the maize feeds our two pigs and brings cash. I can't afford a bad year.

For the winter wheat, I'll sow in mid-October with an improved variety — the same one old Wang used last year, looks like "Liangxing" or something similar. I'll run the rotary tiller over the field first to break up the stubble. For fertilizer, the extension fellow said 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, but two years ago when I tried cutting back to save money the wheat turned yellow at jointing and I lost almost 50 kg per mu. So I'm putting down about 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer — the 18-22-5 kind — as base, and then at jointing in March I'll spread another 25 kg per mu of urea. That should come to around 18 kg nitrogen total, plus some phosphorus and potassium. I know the soil is getting tired, so I don't dare go lower. I'll irrigate three times: once around New Year if the snow is thin, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Water isn't free anymore since they put meters on the wells, so three times is my limit. For pests, I'll spray herbicide once in early spring and another time for insects or rust if I see spots on the leaves.

Come early June, as soon as the wheat is harvested, I have maybe two days to get the summer maize in or the growing season is too short. There is no time to plow — I'll use no-tillage planting with a hybrid maize, probably "Nongda372" like most of the village. I'll put down about 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at planting — the 28-6-6 type — and if the leaves look pale at the big trumpet stage I might topdress a little extra urea, but usually the base is enough. Summer rains help, but if July is dry like last year I'll irrigate twice: once when the tassels come out and once during grain filling. I'll spray herbicide right after sowing, and then insecticide once or twice when the corn borers show up. 

If the weather is normal, I expect about 450 kg per mu from the wheat and 480 kg per mu from the maize. Not a fortune, but steady — enough to eat, enough to sell a bit, and enough to pay for my daughter's high school fees.
